findings.title: LoggerMiddleware silently loses pluginId/endpoint/traceID unless ContextualLoggerMiddleware is composed first
findings.body: The "Plugin Request Completed" log line (the grafana-data-egress audit event) previously included pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, dsUID and traceID explicitly. It now relies entirely on `m.logger.FromContext(ctx)` picking up contextual attributes that were injected by the separate ContextualLoggerMiddleware. Nothing enforces that composition: if LoggerMiddleware is used without ContextualLoggerMiddleware earlier in the chain (e.g. in tests, alternative wire setups, or future reordering of CreateMiddlewares), the audit logs will silently contain no pluginId, endpoint, user or datasource identifiers and no traceID. There is no test covering the LoggerMiddleware output fields after this change to catch such a regression.

findings.title: traceID no longer guaranteed in data-egress log event
findings.body: The old code explicitly appended `traceID` from `tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` to the "Plugin Request Completed" log parameters. The new code drops that and relies on the contextual logger (`FromContext`) to surface a trace ID. Unless `log.WithContextualAttributes`/`ConcreteLogger.FromContext` is guaranteed to attach the trace ID from the context, this removes the traceID field from the grafana-data-egress event, breaking correlation between plugin egress logs and traces. This should be verified or the traceID explicitly re-added.

findings.title: Stream endpoints are not enriched with the contextual logger
findings.body: SubscribeStream, PublishStream and RunStream are passed through without calling instrumentContext, so any downstream logging for streaming requests will lack pluginId/endpoint/dsName/uname. RunStream is a long-lived request where such context is especially valuable. This matches the old behavior for the logger, but since the PR introduces a dedicated middleware whose sole purpose is contextual logging, the omission is now more conspicuous.

findings.title: No tests for the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware
findings.body: A new middleware with non-trivial behavior (attribute selection, nil checks on DataSourceInstanceSettings and User) is added without any test coverage. There is also no test verifying that the LoggerMiddleware's output actually contains the previously-present fields (pluginId, endpoint, traceID, uname, dsName) after the refactor, which is the main behavioral risk of this PR.

findings.title: Test still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware after rename to MetricsMiddleware
findings.body: The middleware was renamed from InstrumentationMiddleware to MetricsMiddleware, but the test function is still called TestInstrumentationMiddleware, which is confusing for anyone searching for tests of the renamed component.
